steps.description:
This walkthrough introduces the four core source files that make up the Alchemist V3 “Core” component and shows where a user or reviewer would begin reading.

- `src/interfaces/IAlchemistV3.sol` – the public facing interface.
- `src/AlchemistV3.sol` – the main state-holding implementation.
- `src/interfaces/IAlchemistV3Position.sol` – interface for the position-tracking NFT.
- `src/AlchemistV3Position.sol` – **ERC-721** contract that mints/burns positions on behalf of AlchemistV3.

The next steps highlight the entry points in each file without digging into internal logic.
The public interface is aggregated into a single type that end users and integrators import.
First two user actions – supplying collateral (deposit) and withdrawing it (withdraw).  Notice that the position is always identified by `tokenId`.
Borrowing against collateral: the `mint` entry point.
Closing or correcting positions – burn, repay, and liquidate are the remaining key user methods.
The concrete implementation – note the contract header and the most important state: totals, external component addresses, and the per-account mapping `_accounts`.
Implementation entry point that matches the interface: `deposit`.
Two internal flow helpers you will see referenced throughout the codebase: `_sync` (per-account state refresh) and `_earmark` (global debt accounting).
Interface for the position NFT – only `mint` and `burn` are needed by `AlchemistV3`.
`AlchemistV3Position` is an ERC-721 enumerable token – it inherits from `OpenZeppelin`’s implementation.
User-visible actions on the NFT: **mint**, **burn** and the on-chain metadata generator `tokenURI`.
The `_update` override automatically resets mint allowances whenever a position NFT changes hands – tying the NFT and core logic together.

You now know where each core contract lives, their high-level purpose, and which methods form the public surface area.  Dive into the full implementations when you need details, starting from the entry points highlighted above.
